chunks: From him, from one who mentioned it, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said:

I went out with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) to Yanbu'. So when he came out, I saw red socks upon him, so I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! What is this, the red socks which I see to be upon you?' So he said: 'Socks which I have taken for the journey, and it is more lasting upon the clay, and the rain, and more load-bearing for it'. I said, 'So shall I take it and wear it?' He said, 'As for during the journey, so yes, and as for during the present, so do not change anything with the black'.

key_terms.خُفّ: Leather sock worn over the foot for ablution

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wearing colored socks during travel versus residence in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practical jurisprudence of wearing leather socks (khuff) for ablution, distinguishing between their utility in travel (safar) and their preference in residence (hadr). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) notes that while red socks are durable for journeys, black socks are superior for daily use, reflecting the scholarly tradition that values both functional necessity and aesthetic modesty in ritual purity. This distinction underscores the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding the conditions under which wiping over socks is valid.
